newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Anwar says ringgit within reasonable range - report.
newsitem.headline: Anwar says ringgit within reasonable range - report.

text.p: Malaysian Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday that the ringgit's exchange rate is within a "reasonable range" despite its sharp fall against the dollar on Monday, the national Bernama news agency reported.

"The currency should reflect the country's strong economic fundamentals, which we feel is still within a reasonable range," he told reporters at the Parliament lobby, when asked whether the ringgit's current range was reasonable.
On what was the reasonable rate was for the ringgit, Anwar said he was not among those who speculate on currencies.
"The government will surely not support anything that leads to speculation," Bernama quoted him as saying.
"We have the responsibility to ensure that the ringgit stays at a reasonable level based on fundamentals of the economy.

"So, if there's excessive speculation, then Bank Negara is responsible to correct the situation, but the situation also changes based on the judgement and sentiment of the market," said Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister.
The ringgit on Monday fell to a 16-month low against the dollar, battered by speculative selling after the recent de-facto devaluations of the Thai baht and the Philippine peso.
